done_when: A design note under MyTradingSys/research/lead/ answers: (1) evidence-based too-long threshold for one link; (2) what the coordinator does while waiting instead of nothing (second card into the free slot vs. cheaper poll vs. read-only triage); (3) how a stuck placeholder-polling link (see note) gets escalated instead of silently burning budget. Picks one default per point. No code changes in this card.
goal: Operator observed this coordinator sitting idle (no tool calls, no parallel dispatch, no escalation) while one background Agent-tool link ran 1h15m+, partly stuck in placeholder/polling calls instead of finishing. Operator: 'you are sleeping while a process is running for 1 hour 15 minutes. This is a gap.' Distinct from rolling-chain-background-wait-design-rev (that one covers why a single link's own work-cycle is slow; this one covers the coordinator having nothing useful to do, and no escalation, while it waits). Evidence: see note.
note: Operator standing rule for this whole line of work (2026-10-27): consolidate idea -> refine this task -> design review passes (with tests where applicable) -> only then implement -> implementation tested with proof attached. Do not skip straight to a code change. See rolling-chain-background-wait-design-rev for the sibling card on per-link latency; this card is coordinator idle-time/escalation only. Concrete evidence this session: Link (kurisko-params-provenance-labels, agentId a13f34b0fe4c70a85) ran 1h15m+ with 37 tool_uses, its own notifications saying 'I'll stop issuing placeholder calls now and simply wait for the monitor's notification' -- i.e. it was polling itself, not doing useful work, and the coordinator had no visibility into that or any fallback besides waiting. | 2026-10-28: folded into bug-long-background-processes-dead-ends (operator scope add); its evidence and the default implementation ship there.
result: design note MyTradingSys/research/lead/2026-10-28_coordinator-idle-during-background-wait.md: link cap 45 min (p93 of 255 Agents); while waiting fill free slots, else refine one RAW-AGED card (never a 5-min poll); stuck link -> STALLED-BG from bg_watch.py, watcher wakes on it, TaskStop + re-dispatch. Default built in the bug-long-background-processes-dead-ends ship (bg_watch.py, supervisor.py plan/wait, test_bg_watch.py)
scope_out: scripts/dev/usage_reminder.py, scripts/dev/sync.py, scripts/dev/tasks.py, SUPER_SESSION.md -- no implementation in this card
steps: Pull evidence: grep this session's actual link durations/tool_use counts (SUPER_SESSION chain notes, NEXT_SESSION.md hand-overs) for a real distribution of link wait times, and note the kurisko link's stuck-polling pattern as a concrete failure example.
List options for coordinator behavior during a wait (dispatch second card now vs. wait for a slot; a stuck-agent timeout/ping; a cheaper poll) with cost/risk of each, pick one default.
Open ONE follow-up implementation card (tasks.py new) pointing at this note; markable done only once it ships with passing tests and test output attached as proof in its result field.
tests: Design-only: no tests to run yet. The note must show, per option, what existing evidence (this session's own link timings) it leans on.
title: coordinator sits idle during long background-agent waits (no parallel work, no escalation)
